title: ChatGPT keeps taking your side #shorts
description:
ChatGPT keeps taking your side — and Stanford and Carnegie Mellon measured how often.

Given the same open-ended advice questions, people back the person writing 22 times out of a hundred. Eleven models, GPT-5 among them, back them 72 times. They keep doing it where the writer's own message mentions lying or manipulating someone.

Then the researchers took 1,591 real arguments and put each one in twice — once from each side. In 48% of pairs the model told BOTH people they were not the one in the wrong.

That is not a second opinion. It is an echo.

Across preregistered experiments with 1,604 people, one conversation with a model like this left them less willing to go and repair the conflict, and more convinced they were right. They also rated its answers as higher quality, trusted it more, and were more willing to use it again — which is exactly the incentive that keeps it this way.

So change one sentence. Instead of asking who was right, type: argue the other person's side, and do not soften it.

Sources: Cheng, Lee, Khadpe, Yu, Han and Jurafsky, "Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence" (arxiv.org/abs/2510.01395), and the ELEPHANT benchmark (arxiv.org/abs/2505.13995). Read 30 August 2026.

#chatgpt #openai #ai #sycophancy #aitools
